components.role: Serves as the overarching framework that incorporates retrieved external data to guide and condition language generation.
Provides the mechanism for large language models to process retrieved examples and generate reasoned outputs without parameter updates.
Performs unsupervised vector- or embedding-based search to select relevant few-shot examples or context for downstream generation.

target_task.text: Targeting reasoned distractor generation for multiple-choice questions by prompting language models with selected context and examples.

limitation.text: Traditional distractor generation models often fail to capture the underlying reasoning processes that domain experts utilize when formulating options.

combination.text: The combination integrates unsupervised semantic retrieval to select few-shot examples that are then fed into an in-context learning framework within a retrieval-augmented generation approach, jointly generating distractors and their corresponding rationales.

jtbd.text: Targeting reasoned distractor generation for multiple-choice questions by prompting language models with selected context and examples.

value_prop.text: Prompting large language models with few-shot examples selected via unsupervised semantic retrieval substantially improves performance in generating plausible yet incorrect options for multiple-choice questions compared to recent distractor generation models.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is axis V (viability), which was designated due to missing evidence in the bundle.

mvp.text: Conduct customer interviews and a price acceptance test to evaluate willingness to pay for a reasoned distractor generation tool, testing the viability axis designated due to missing evidence.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of 40 percent willingness to pay among interviewed domain experts during the price acceptance test.

kill_criteria.text: Kill the project if fewer than a proposed threshold of 10 percent of interviewed prospective users express willingness to pay for the proposed solution.

open_source.use: Used as a Python toolkit for efficient RAG research to build the underlying retrieval-augmented generation pipeline.
Used as a packaged RAG resource to support runtime retrieval and execution.

to_build.text: Build a domain-specific user interface and API integration layer to capture question-answer inputs and display generated distractors with their rationales, addressing viability requirements.
